He wagered a soul on the roll of a die, believing it was his to bet. As the ivory settled, the grasping hands materialized, waiting to collect the true debt.
It was not the bite of the beast that felled the giant, but a single, perfect cut from a forgotten promise.

When you enter the arena, remember you are part of the installation. Perform with vigor.

The more spectacular your... decommissioning of the other exhibits... the more valuable the echoes you'll yield for my collection.

Haggle? With me?

My good fellow, I have acquired treasures from ruins history itself has forgotten.

My price is the final word.

I am the Curator.

You are standing inside my masterpiece.

Marvelous, aren't they?

The zombies provide such a wonderful sense of physicality.

The ghosts, on the other hand, offer a more... ethereal aesthetic.

A balanced collection needs both.

Ah. You're the one he sent. Of course you are. Try Honesty never comes himself when pride might be spared by distance.

Yes, I kept the Brass Bout Bell. He lost it fairly, however loudly he may remember otherwise. A fountain was used, the terms were broken, and the bout ceased to be a bout at all.

He believes a cheering crowd can correct a ruined condition. He is wrong. Frequently, and with style.

Still, I am told you performed well. Better than most of the meat he throws into that pit. That gives me hope.

So take the bell. Not as settlement of his grievance, but as an investment in yours.

The Brass Bout Bell is yours now.

Take it back to Try Honesty. I am certain he will mistake retrieval for vindication.

I provide the tools for the exhibits to... refine themselves.

I accept the resonant echoes left behind by the... decommissioned performers... and in return, I lend out superior artifacts to those who show promise.

You are in the Carrion Ascension.

The centerpiece of my exhibition on mortal transience and posthumous endeavor.

The fights below are a... dynamic sculpture. A study in conflict.

I am the Curator.

This crypt, this arena, the very echoes that cling to the air... all of it is part of my permanent collection.

You are standing inside my masterpiece.

Cynthia: Someone's here, Elias. Do you feel it? They feel... real.
Elias: I know... The whole place felt it, sister.
Cynthia: Do you think they've come for us?
Elias: If they have, the Warden will find them first.

Cynthia: They're inside. Elias... they really went in. Why would it let them in?
Elias: It shouldn't have... Maybe it wants something from them.
Cynthia: That's what worries me.

Cynthia: They're really going down there?
Elias: Hm. Seems so.
Cynthia: The Warden must think highly of them... if he's letting them near Father's arena.
Elias: I don't think that's why he let them through.
Cynthia: Then we'll see what he wants with them.

Careful with the cards you clutch so tightly. Some of their threads run deeper than this crypt, down past the bedrock, into a place the church stopped naming.

She listens there. She likes curious hands.

In the records, the Callas look immaculate: the family appointed to stand between the church and the place below, after the first archivist - the one they bound down there - the one that had to be contained.

The wards beneath don't listen to prayers. They listen to blood. Callas blood opens doors other people can only die in front of.

So the church called it duty. Privilege. Legacy.

She reads it differently. To her, the Callas line has always been a promise: that where the margins of her own bloodline bled into theirs, a Callas girl would be born more key than child - ink and Callas blood braided into a vessel made to fit the one below.

Careful with the cards you clutch so tightly. Some of their threads run deeper than this crypt, down past the bedrock, into a place the church stopped naming.

She listens there. She likes curious hands.

You call them undying.

I see bodies whose stories were cut wrong and stitched back by a will that refuses endings.

Some of what's wrong here is older than that. Those people died the way people are meant to.

Flesh to soil, breath to silence. It's their souls that never made it out - thin, stubborn echoes pinned here, because this estate and the place below drink from the same poisoned vein.

The others are different. They went down into the place below and left too much of themselves within her reach.

What crawled back up wears their meat, but there isn't a story inside anymore... just hunger, hanging off a borrowed thread.

Then we ask water to remember what it was before it learned to bargain.

Find the vial Marlowe kept. Untouched grace can rinse noise from a vision without teaching it to bite back.

There. The thread finds its pattern again.

The static recedes, and the image of the Sanctum begins to gather back into shape. You did well.

On the surface?

Just pictures, numbers, promises. Underneath, they're pages torn from lives that already happened - memories that slipped the binding.

Each card is an echo of a story you never got to live. When you hand me a set, I press that story into one shape and give it a body again.

You call it an item.
I call it... closure.

Anywhere the place below brushes against the surface.

They cling to things that kept moving after their story should have stopped, and to those who walked too far into the wrong corridors and didn't come back whole.

If a road feels like it's straying toward the depths, watch what falls there.

The cards are drawn to that kind of ruin.

Who am I...?

That depends which one of you is asking.

Up here they write it as Lyra, Weaver of Threads. Sounds tidy, doesn't it?

As if any of this was done on purpose.

I listen to the loose strands that got caught in your cards - the bits of you that almost were, or were once already.

I give them something solid to become, and you walk away thinking it was just a trade.

As for who I was before...

She remembers better than I do.

The one below.

I try not to use her name; it has a habit of answering back.

She was the one who filed other people's truths into neat little rows. An archivist, breathing dust and ink, lingering in the forbidden margins no one was meant to read.

Then the words stopped lying still for her. They slipped off the page, wound themselves around her thoughts... and a few important stitches came loose.

The church called it heresy. The place below called it an opening.

Now she's more pull than person - a will moving along the deeper threads, looking for a loose one like yours to tug.

I don't use her name. Names are doorhandles, and she's very good at turning them.
Lyra's transmutation is not available right now.
What kind of deals does it offer?

Controlling it? Good heavens, no.

I simply understand its manners better than most.
My dear friend, everyone uses something. Tools, faith, fear, other people. I am merely more polite about it.

Excellent. The fountain is waiting, and it adores decisive customers.

Take one bargain. Any one. Return when the water has marked the transaction, and I will release the vial.

There we are. Paid in consequence, sealed by the fountain, witnessed by a man of impeccable bookkeeping.

Take the vial to Lyra. And do try to remember who kept it safe all these years.

Ah, a customer. Or a pilgrim. Hard to tell these days.

Either way, welcome.
Back again? Wonderful. I was beginning to worry you had developed caution.
Come to bargain, or merely to stare at the consequences?
Careful near the water. It has a talent for overhearing desire.
Ah. My favorite kind of visitor. Alive, curious, and not yet sufficiently warned.

Useful ones. Dangerous ones. The sort people swear they would never accept, until they need them badly enough.

Strength for frailty. Fortune for hunger. Clarity for something you may miss only after it is gone.
Most bargains do, when described honestly.

Once? A holy little thing, I am told. Graceful, generous, terribly inefficient.

Now? It has matured.
A blessing for a consequence. That is how the fountain speaks now.
<accent>Marlowe Veyne</accent>. Collector of rare opportunities, negotiator of regrettable wishes, and, on better days, a perfectly respectable gentleman.
Charlatan is such an ugly word. I prefer... <accent>specialist in selective truths</accent>.

Because this is where people come when prayer has failed, coin has failed, and good sense has failed most of all.

And because the fountain and I have an understanding.
I bring it the desperate. It reminds them that nothing worth having arrives cleanly.
That sounds like a lot of words for charlatan.

Cynthia, if Mr. Klaus sees you out late again... oh.

You're someone else. Forgive me.

The water keeps returning the wrong reflections.

Cynthia, if Mr. Klaus sees you out late again... oh.

You're someone else. Forgive me.

The water keeps returning the wrong reflections.

No... no, I'm fine.

I have everything I need.

But... if you do see Julian, tell him I'll be waiting.

Just a little longer.

Of course.

The water's better company, anyway.

The name is Melora.

I work the kitchens.

Sometimes I help with the little ones when the mistress isn't looking.

Oh, I like it here.

It's quiet.

The water listens better than people do.
I found something in the coffin!

You woke with the sound of a bell in your head.
In the dream, you saw a ruined church beneath a dead sky. Its doors stood open.
Below the floorboards, candlelight flickered.
You do not know why it matters.
But a church may still mean shelter, supplies, or answers.

Marlowe has the Vial of Unspoiled Grace, and no intention of releasing it for something as cheap as gratitude. He calls the fountain honest: one blessing, one consequence, every miracle properly accounted for. Accept one bargain from the fountain, then return to Marlowe and collect the vial.

Lyra's visions of the Sanctum are drowning in corrupted divine noise. The fountain's current waters would only turn memory into a bargain. Marlowe holds a Vial of Unspoiled Grace, drawn before the curse. Find him by the courtyard fountain behind Callas Manor and recover it.

Serevine returns the Sanctified Bell to you,
not as a trophy, but with a purpose.
She believes the altar in the chamber beside her was made to receive relics such as this, allowing their sacred influence to endure while bound within it.
Place the Sanctified Bell into the relic altar, then return to Serevine.
Place the <accent>Sanctified Bell</accent> into the <accent>relic altar</accent>

Serevine believes the bell seen in your dream may be the Sanctified Bell, a sacred Valerian relic once sealed somewhere beneath Cedar Hill Church. If she is right, then your dream was no mere imagining.
Descend deeper into the church cellars, uncover the hidden reliquary, recover the Sanctified Bell, and return it to Serevine.

Serevine has exhausted the church's surviving records of the Sanctuary. They confirm that it once existed, but reveal nothing of its location, its purpose, or the reason it was hidden. The Callas family may have preserved what the church concealed.
Travel to Callas Manor and uncover any record they left behind concerning the Sanctuary.

Silas has heard the dead of House Callas stirring within their family cemetery. The wards etched upon their stone coffins are failing, leaving their rest exposed to whatever stirs below.
Take the warding kit, repair the broken wards, and return to Silas once the graves have fallen silent.

Silas believes you have earned an introduction. With the Regal Hatch Key in hand, the way to the Carrion Ascension now lies open.
Beneath the opposite crypt waits an arena few living souls are invited to see.
Descend through the hatch and present your invitation to Try Honesty.

Silas has entrusted you with a grim task. The Mother's Crypt is poisoned by a sorrow that has festered into rage, unsettling the peace of the graveyard. He has given you the key, and charged you to enter the crypt, find the source of the turmoil, and put it to rest by any means necessary.

You heard a voice near the Callas Family Cemetery...

"Ah, a living soul... a rare and welcome sight these days. If you have a moment for an old warden, come, let us speak."

Find the source of the voice among the graves, and learn what stirs there.

Explore the Estate. While the right path leads to the old graveyard, the left fork remains largely unexplored.
It winds past the estate's overgrown greenhouse and down toward the waterline. Perhaps the servants who once walked this route knew secrets their masters had long since forgotten.

Try Honesty is not done with you yet.
The crowd has seen you survive. Now they want to know whether you can win without leaning on the fountain like a wounded noble at a garden party.
Complete one full arena match without using the fountain, then return to Try Honesty.

Try Honesty has accepted your invitation,
though not without making a spectacle of it.
The Carrion Ascension does not hand out glory freely. Step into the arena, survive one full match, and return to Try Honesty with your dignity mostly intact.

Try Honesty has decided your survival may yet be useful. An old wager with the Curator ended poorly after a match was soured by technicalities, excuses, and one very inconvenient fountain.
Ask the Curator about the wager, recover the Brass Bout Bell, and return it to Try Honesty.
The spirits... they're finally at peace.
The old warden... what tales he must hold.
The fountain broke the challenge. I will have to try again.
I made it through the arena.
The bell is back where it belongs.

Stop right there. Not a step closer!
...Oh. A person. And alive?
Wonderful. Alarming, but wonderful.
Come in, then. A fellow explorer, I hope.

Sorry. You startled me half to death, which is very rude in a place already full of death.
I'm Serevine, Valerian scholar, temporary cellar resident, and currently very grateful you are not trying to eat me.

Oh, it worked! There is something different about you now. A steadiness, perhaps... as though the Bell has finally found its proper bearer. Leave it upon the altar, and I believe its blessing will remain with you.
Is that a map of Callas Manor?
Any idea why the dead walk?
I saw this church in a dream

It is. Remarkable, isn't it?

Every wing, every garden path, even the servants' passages have been recorded in extraordinary detail.

I had expected a parish sketch. This is something far more deliberate.

Though it has one rather curious omission.

The records place Valerian's first sanctuary somewhere beneath the estate.

Yet this map makes no mention of it at all.

For a place of such importance to be absent from a map this precise... I find it very difficult to believe that was an oversight.

Nothing I could honestly call an answer.

But I have found records of visits to a Valerian sanctuary on the Callas estate. Supposedly, the first sanctuary ever raised in His name.

If that is true, it is extraordinary. Thousands of years of history, doctrine, relics... perhaps even accounts from the founding of the faith itself.

I confess, I was rather thrilled when I first understood what I was reading.

Then I reached the later entries. The visits become fewer. People return from the sanctuary described as distant... vacant... diminished.

One account says a man came back breathing, walking, and speaking... yet his wife insisted that whatever returned from beneath the estate was no longer her husband.

I would very much like to dismiss it as frightened superstition. Given what is wandering outside, that has become rather difficult.

If there is an answer beneath the Callas estate, I think we ought to find it.

This church? Before you had ever set foot inside it?
How extraordinary.

Forgive me. I imagine it was rather less extraordinary to experience.

Dreams of sacred sites do appear in old Valerian studies, though never in any account I considered reliable.

There is one detail those accounts repeat with peculiar consistency.

Tell me, did you hear a bell?

You did?
Then I may owe several long-dead scholars a sincere apology.

I had always assumed they were describing a symbol, not an actual phenomenon.

Judging by the state of the steeples, I sincerely doubt the tower bell has rung for a very long time.

Yet the accounts describe a bell heard in sleep, calling the living toward sacred ground.

I thought it devotional allegory.

Now you are standing here, in the very church those accounts describe. Which makes this considerably more important than I had hoped.

Take it. Not as a trophy, but with a purpose.

The altar in the nearby chamber was made to receive relics such as this. If the bell is placed there, its influence may endure without being carried in your hands.

Then it worked. There is something steadier in the air now, as though the Bell has finally found its proper bearer.

Leave it upon the altar, and I believe its blessing will remain with you.

Then we should treat your dream as evidence, however inconvenient that may be.

The accounts speak of a bell beneath holy ground. If the relic is here, it will not have been left in any ordinary chamber.

Descend below the church. Find what the Valerians sealed away, and bring the bell to me before you bind it to anything.

You found it. Valerian's Bell... and not merely a story after all.

There is a sanctified mark beneath the tarnish. Give me a moment with it. If the old rite still answers, I can return it to you as something more than salvage.

The church records have taken us as far as they can.

If the Callas family concealed what the Church could not admit, their manor may still hold the missing account. Recover any record they left behind concerning the Sanctuary.

This is exactly what I feared, and exactly what I needed.

The Callas record gives shape to the omission. Whatever lies beneath that estate was not forgotten. It was deliberately hidden.

I had hoped it was only a hidden archive. The scrolls, the sealed records, the fireplace kept for long nights of study... those I can understand.

Though judging by the dust, no one has studied here in centuries.

The cages in the corridor are rather harder to explain. Rust, brittle leather, dust thick enough to bury a confession.

Whatever happened here, it happened long before the dead began walking.

There are restraints here. Instruments meant for questioning, if one wishes to be charitable.

Whatever was recorded in this room, I do not think it was always offered willingly.

That is the part I find most troubling. The restraints bear Valerian seals. The records beside them carry the same insignia.

Whoever used this place was not hiding from the Church. They were acting in its name.

I study Valerian relics, sacred sites, and the history people usually find more comfortable leaving buried.

I came to Cedar Hill after hearing the rather extraordinary accounts surrounding Callas Manor.

My superiors thought the matter warranted investigation.

Truthfully, I would have come whether they asked or not.
The Shattered Visage shatters, saving you from death!
That should be all of them. Silas should know.
This grave seal is intact. No correction needed.
The ward holds here. Leave this grave be.
No corruption here. This seal is already correct.
Corrupted seal found. Use Silas' kit to correct it.
This ward is inverted. Correct this grave seal.
The seal is broken here. This grave needs correction.
I should examine the seal first.
I need Silas' seal kit for this.
The seal settles. {count} still feel unstable.
Greetings, traveler. I am <accent>Silas</accent>, the warden of this place. It is not often I receive visitors who still draw breath.
Ah, a living soul... a rare and welcome sight these days. If you have a moment for an old warden, come, let us speak.

Take the kit. Its tools are modest, but they remember the shape of the old wards.

Examine the grave seals throughout the cemetery. If one answers wrong, correct it before the unrest spreads.

Yes... I can feel it. The stones are quieter now.

You have given the dead a kindness, and the living a little more time.

Perhaps. The wards around this cemetery have begun to fray in ways they should not.

If you are willing, I would ask you to inspect the grave seals, correct what has been miswritten, and return before the unrest deepens.
Greetings, traveler. I am <accent>Silas</accent>, the warden of this place. It is not often I receive visitors who still draw breath.

Then the way is open. Take this invitation.

The place across the grounds will not welcome the living easily, but it should recognize the warden's seal.

I see you have taken an interest in the plight of this place. Thank you.

The Mother's Crypt holds a sorrow that has festered into rage.

It disturbs the peace of this entire ground.

Take this key. Enter, and pacify the source of the turmoil.

The crypt is still at last.

Whatever pain was bound below has loosened its grip. Rest may return to this ground.

My name is Silas.

I am the keeper of this graveyard, a warden of memories and a tender of final rest.

I have watched over these stones for longer than I care to recall, ensuring the peace of those who reside here.

This is my purpose.

The living have their bustling cities, and the departed... have this.

Someone must ensure their slumber is not disturbed by the... restless energies that cling to Callas Manor.

It is a quiet duty, but a necessary one.

Enjoy? That's the word mortals use when someone finally does what they were made for.

The Curator and I once placed a gentleman's wager. A relic against the outcome of a bout. Then the match soured, a fountain was touched, and that shrivelled little priest of order decided the rules had been violated.

I say a fighter still breathing is a fighter still in the contest. He says otherwise. Naturally, he wrote the conclusion down and called it truth.

So he kept my stake. The Brass Bout Bell. Without it, the pit is mere spectacle. With it, the bout is sanctioned.

Go to him. Tell him I want the bell returned.
